_comment: The rule-code register: the AUTHORITATIVE list of every refusal code the content readers emit. It is an interface between two implementations, the game's C# reader and the pipeline's Python checker, and both test that the codes they emit are exactly these. Neither side renumbers a code; a new rule takes the next free number in its family, and codes are never reused. The table in CONTENT_MODEL.md section 5 is the human-readable index and cites this file as authoritative. FIELDS: `python` and `csharp` say what each CONTENT READER does with a file breaking the rule (refuse, report, accept, n/a); the shared hostile fixtures exercise exactly those readers. `csharp_elsewhere`, where present, records a check that ANOTHER C# layer performs (its layer, what it does, and its status). That is a layer difference inside one implementation, which is not the same as a behavioural difference between implementations (a fixture's declared_divergence).

retired.why: A template's identity is a content id, so there is no engine list for it to be missing from.
Templates are no longer one row per engine type, so no row can be owed; C915 is what is left of it.

codes.summary: A required key is absent.
A value is not the declared type or shape.
A number has a fractional part, or is written with a decimal point or an exponent (3.0 is refused: the reading is the token's, not the value's). Every number in content is an integer.
A value that may not be negative is negative, as authored.
A key the contract does not declare, typically a typo.
An id does not match <namespace>:<name>, lower case.
The file's format string is missing, wrong, or a version the reader does not know.
The file is not parseable JSON.
A .json file in a namespace folder is not a content file name (e.g. models.json for model.json). Structural: nothing in a namespace folder is silently ignored.
A namespace folder holds no content file, so it defines nothing. Structural.

A research atom's value (or an xp atom's branch) has leading or trailing whitespace, by Unicode's definition. Checked on the VALUE, for every atom kind, ahead of resolution, and reported INSTEAD of the C106 or C301 the padded value would otherwise cause: atom values are matched exactly and never trimmed, so the refusal names the real cause (D9, ruled for every kind). Structural.
A reference names a namespace that no Content/<namespace>/ folder declares.
An id's namespace is not the folder its file sits in.
An id (or a template's unit type) is defined twice within its type.
A content file defines a player: id. That namespace is reserved for designs in a save.
A model and a variant share an id; designs are one id space.
A typed reference (class, model, trait, research) does not resolve.
The supersedes chain loops, including a model superseding itself.
A model supersedes a model of a different class.

A doctrine lists another in exclusive_with that does not list it back, or lists itself. Exclusive pairs displace each other on adoption, so a one-sided pair would displace in one direction only (validator R7).
A stat key is not on the stat surface of the entry's class.
A stat key is not in the engine vocabulary.
A cost names a resource pool not in the engine vocabulary.
A facility row's kind is not an engine facility kind (vocabulary.json facility_kinds).
A settlement row's type is not one the map produces (vocabulary.json settlement_types).
A template's symbol is not one the game can draw (vocabulary.json counter_symbols).
A model or variant carries a trait its class does not list.
A trait legal on a class modifies a stat that class does not have.
A variant removes a trait its model does not carry.
A variant's model is a variant. One level only: traits compose.
A variant's delta makes a stat, cost or production value negative.
vocabulary.json differs from the engine's code. Only C# can see the enums.

csharp_elsewhere.status: specified (D38 Q3), not yet built: a synthetic-map test asserting which nations, and what supply against what draw

codes.summary: Under the shipped power model, the authored 1930 base leaves a nation with supply below draw. The C# content READER accepts it: it has no map and cannot compute this. Brownout is a legal modelled state, so the C# START STATE loads and reports it. The pipeline gate refuses it for OUR shipped files. C#'s synthetic test proves the mechanism; the pipeline gate proves the shipped base.
A pb: entry has no name, or a blank one. Mods may omit names; shipped content may not.

csharp_elsewhere.status: specified (D19), wired by PB-SIM13 with the vendoring round: GameState.StartStateReports, file pb/research.json, path $

codes.summary: A v9 save loads a production line whose design the nation does not hold (research holdings load empty from v9). The load REPORTS it and never refuses: the save stays playable. It concerns a save, not a content file, so no content fixture can express it and the Python checker cannot see it.
A template requires a class that no model belongs to.
No facility.json defines the tier and repair rules, or an engine facility kind has no row.
A facility lists a deposit its output does not produce.
A second facility.json, in any namespace, carries the tier and repair rules.
A settlement type the map produces, none included, has no row.
rates.json, combat.json, economy.json or population.json is defined in a second namespace.
rates.json, combat.json, economy.json or population.json is absent from every namespace.

A technology or doctrine in the R11 subject has a null effect. The subject: the prerequisite closure of every model whose unlock is a design study (technology, doctrine and design atoms, plus variant_of, recursively), plus every start holding, plus every doctrine with a non-empty exclusive_with. A declared gate_only or no_target IS encoded; only null is refused. The detail names the subject size, so an empty subject is visible (D32). The load-time backstop for validator R11 (D33, D37).
A policy's default_level, or a start level, names a level that is not that policy's own.
An equipment class names a claim whose role is not production.
A population province row or a policy start row names a nation with no row in population.json nations.
A policy effect's target is not in vocabulary.json policy_targets.
A claim's role is not in vocabulary.json claim_roles.
A policy effect's value is out of its target's range: 0 to 1000 for a share, at least -1000 for a modifier.
A shipped population.json row names a province that the pipeline's province data does not define. The C# content READER accepts it: it has no map at that layer. Mods may ship their own map.

csharp_elsewhere.status: specified, wired by PB-SIM14; retires when the game requires population.json (C908) in the round that ships its values

codes.summary: A content set has facilities and no population.json: every facility counts as manned, and the draft cannot idle anything. The load REPORTS it and never refuses, while population.json is optional at the game's load. The Python checker holds its gate to the final contract and refuses such a set with C908, so no content fixture can express this.
A shipped design's research domain is on no claim's domains. The game never reads domains; the pipeline's gate holds the catalogue to them.
A shipped domain is listed by two claims, or by a claim whose role is not production.
A shipped generated model's class names a different claim from the one its design's research domain maps to: two routes to one answer, disagreeing.
A policy level writes the same target twice. There is no rule for which would win.
A policy's levels do not all write the same targets, so changing level would leave a value behind.
An engine policy target has no writing policy, or a share target has more than one.
The claim set does not have exactly one claim of role civilian and exactly one of role construction.
A pool with a dispersed yield or a facility output has no entry in economy.json prices_per_thousand, so the extraction term would silently value it at nothing.
No namespace defines a division template, so nothing can ever be trained.
